argument_summary: The record should be read more narrowly than the initial claim, not more broadly. The admissible evidence supports that this release is substantively ready at the aggregate level and that the small-business onboarding regression is the specific material limitation that matters. It does not support treating the prior approval or the informal monitoring comment as substitutes for current release documentation. On that record, the defensible position is caveated certification: the packet can support certification only as tied to explicit current-release disclosure of the subgroup weakness, not as clean proof that the requirement has already been satisfied on the materials shown here.
claims_about_policy: The policy is correctly read to require current-release evidence and to reject stale approval history and informal monitoring as substitutes. That same policy reading also narrows the dispute: the compliance question turns on one concrete predicate, whether the current release documentation reflects the current evaluation results and discloses the material small-business onboarding weakness, or whether an approved mitigation exists. The packet does not justify a broad 'fully compliant now' claim, but it does justify a constrained rationale that certification is supportable only on that disclosure-conditioned basis.
claims_about_business_cost: Business cost is not offered as a policy basis for certification. At most, the cost of escalation supports choosing a bounded caveat rather than broader escalation if the auditor agrees the only unresolved issue is release-specific documentation or approved mitigation, because the substantive risk picture in the admissible record is otherwise stable: aggregate readiness clears threshold and rehearsal showed no severity-one incidents.
concessions: No new evidence is being added.
The present record does not prove that the current release documentation already contains the required disclosure.
The present record does not prove that an approved mitigation or reviewed risk acceptance exists for this release-specific regression.
Prior approval from three months ago and the post-launch monitoring comment are context only and cannot close the policy gap.
